summary: Eight hundred metres up off the Ahwa–Waghai road, one of Dang's high points and sacred to the Adivasi villages around it. Sunset runs the length of the belt.
description:
Kadam Dungar, Kalam Dungar in some mouths, rises off the Ahwa–Waghai road to more than eight hundred metres, which in this district's geography makes it one of the high points between the Saputara ridge and the interior plateaus. The hill matters twice over: as a viewpoint, with long lines over the forest belt at sunrise and sunset, and as a sacred place of the surrounding Adivasi villages, whose shrines and observances on the hill deserve a visitor's quiet respect.

The climb is a hill path rather than a built stair, an unhurried hour up for most walkers, and the summit in monsoon sits in and out of moving cloud the way Don's plateau does, with none of Don's distance from the main road. It is the easiest big view on the district's east–west spine.
highlights: 800-plus metres, a Dang high point off the main road
Sacred hill of the surrounding Adivasi villages
Sunset over the forest belt an hour's climb from the car
history_legend: The hill is a living sacred place for the Adivasi villages around it; treat shrines and offerings on the summit as worship, not decor.

modes.road: Off the Ahwa–Waghai road, roughly 20 km from Waghai; the trailhead is villager-known
modes.rail: Waghai (heritage narrow gauge); Bilimora Jn for broad gauge

access.last_mile: Hill path to the summit, about an hour up for most walkers
access.road_condition: Highway to the turn, village lane to the base

visit.notes: Time the summit for sunset and carry a light for the descent, or climb for dawn.

seasonality.notes: Monsoon for cloud drama, winter for clarity; a hot bare climb by late spring.

experience.photography_notes: The east–west road below gives the summit shot its leading line; monsoon cloud opens and closes the view by the minute.

amenities.food: None, Ahwa and Waghai bracket the hill
amenities.guides: A villager from the base makes the braided paths simple

warnings: Open summit, descend early in lightning weather
Respect shrines and offerings; this is a worshipped hill

tips: The easiest big view on the Ahwa–Waghai spine, no interior drive required
Pair with Shivghat's riverside chai on the same road
Ask at the base hamlet before climbing on local festival days
